metadata.title: Testing Low-Acceleration Gravitational Dynamics and the Galactic External Field Effect in Gaia DR3 Wide Binaries via Unified Phase Dynamics
metadata.description:
Recent astrometric measurements of wide binary star systems in the solar neighborhood from the Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) have revealed a statistically decisive breakdown of standard Newtonian dynamics at projected separations s > 2,000 AU, where internal accelerations drop below the cosmic threshold a0 ≈ 1.2 × 10−10 m/s2. Pure Newtonian gravity is rejected by the observational kinematics at greater than 5σ (χ2/dof = 10.97).

Simultaneously, we demonstrate that the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) halo hypothesis is physically incapable of explaining this anomaly, suffering from an insurmountable 9,585× mass deficit on AU scales (MDM / Mtot ∼ 2.5 × 10−5 at s = 20,000 AU). While isolated modified gravity theories predict an unconstrained divergence α = g/gN ∝ s (χ2/dof = 26.82), the Unified Phase Dynamics of Feynman Path Contours rigorously accounts for the background gravitational acceleration of the Milky Way galaxy (gext ≈ 2.166 × 10−10 m/s2, eenv = gext/a0 ≈ 1.804).

By performing an exact 3D orientation-averaged integration of the non-linear vacuum phase polarization tensor, we deduce an analytical asymptotic acceleration plateau:

αasymp = ν(eenv) + ⅓ eenv ν'(eenv) ≈ 1.2462   (+24.6% force boost)

corresponding to an asymptotic orbital velocity ratio γv,asymp = √αasymp ≈ 1.1163. This zero-parameter deductive derivation achieves excellent concordance with the Gaia DR3 binned observational dataset (χ2/dof = 3.05), resolving the controversy between pure Newton and unconstrained MOND, and providing direct empirical evidence for emergent phase-current gravitation within the Milky Way disk.
